Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

more adverb

also would you like more, more of, more than, some more, nothing more

classical

Hor. S. 2.6.4: nīl amplius ōrō

amplius

adverb

more, any more (of something offered again)

Other words

  • plūs, plūris n. + gen. — more (of): more food, more time

    noun in the singular, with a partitive genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 66: eō plūs viāticī quaerere; Publil. Sent. C 22: plūs vult quam licet

    “More of” a thing is plūs with a genitive: plūs viāticī, more provisions; “more than”, plūs quam. With verbs and adjectives, see more (to a greater degree).

  • plūrēs, plūra — more (in number): more people, more things

    adjective, plural; gen. plūrium · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.6.2: sed plūra scrībēmus aliās; Phaedr. 2.3.7: successus improbōrum plūrēs allicit

Examples

  • Vīs amplius?

    Would you like more?composed

  • Jam satis est.

    That’s enough now.composed

  • bene est. nīl amplius ōrō

    it is good. I ask for nothing moreHor. S. 2.6.4

  • sed plūra scrībēmus aliās

    but I’ll write more another timeCic. Fam. 7.6.2

  • successus improbōrum plūrēs allicit

    the success of the wicked lures more people onPhaedr. 2.3.7

  • Cui plūs licet quam pār est, plūs vult quam licet.

    Allow someone more than is fair, and he wants more than is allowed.Publil. Sent. C 22

See also be hungry, more, further, less.
